name: Zedekiah
overview: Zedekiah was a male Aaronic priest from the tribe of Levi, named on the sealed document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27. His role as an Aaronic priest highlights his connection to the priestly lineage and religious duties within Israel's worship system. The brief note of his inclusion on this document underscores his recognized status among the faithful leaders of his time.
namesAndTitles: The proper name Zedekiah means 'y-h-v-h is [my] righteousness,' reflecting a theologically rich declaration of God's justice and character. This name is recorded in Nehemiah 10:1 and was not given directly by God but carries a significant meaning consistent with the faith of Israel.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Zedekiah as a descendant of Aaron, indicating his priestly heritage and lineage. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are documented in the given facts, so his familial connections outside this priestly descent remain unspecified.
scriptureSignificance: Zedekiah's significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest named among the covenant community leaders who committed themselves to God's law, as noted in Nehemiah. His priestly identity ties him to the spiritual leadership of Israel, affirming the importance of faithful service in God's covenant community. Although additional historical details about his reign and actions are known from other sources, the facts here emphasize his priestly heritage and faithful inclusion in a solemn covenant renewal.
